When the world reshapes, where does a cell of it go? skin : it stays on its cube of the body, and the bends sweep back through it. space : it stays where it is in space, and the world leaves it behind, a cube a step.

body
retrace carry

Where does your body lie on the new world? retrace : your head keeps its cell and your body is laid back down behind it by its own turns. carry : every cell of you is carried over like the ground, and you're cut wherever two stop touching.

when cut
world keeps world shrinks

The world is as long as you. Cut off part of you and does it lose those cubes too, off its tail end, ground and all? If your head was on them, you fall.

no ground
you fall you slide

When the world shrinks from under your head: do you fall, or does its tail end pull you in with it, onto its new cap? (Cascade plays with the world shrinking and you sliding.)

a bite
bites off kills

grain
fine medium coarse

How many cells across each face of a cube of world: 3, 2 or 1. Coarser is a more zoomed-out game: the world is nearer your own size and shape, so it's tighter, and a bend has fewer ways round you (measured: 1.7, 2.7 and 8 cuts per 100 steps). At 1, every step crosses a fold, so every step is a pitch and the world coils up and down in 3D.

time
slows with bends steady

The more of the world is bent, the more of it changes under you every step (each bend moves a cube a step). With time slowing, a step takes longer the more of the world bends: full speed up to a fifth of it, twice as long when all of it does, eased in and out. Curling up buys you time, and the bends that buy it are the ones that cut you.

speed
slow normal fast

Changing a rule starts a fresh run on the same seed. The URL keeps your rules, so a link reproduces the lab.

back to it

games.mino.mobi · molt · a lab

OUROBOROS

In Molt you dive into your body and it becomes the next
world. Here there's no diving: the world is your body, right now .
One cube of world for every cell of you. Every turn you make becomes a
bend at the world's head, and every bend slides back along it, the way
a snake's body slides through the bends its head made. Eat, and you and
the world grow together.

So the ground moves. When a bend sweeps under you your body can no
longer lie the way it did, and where it can't, you're cut : the
tail falls off and lies there as food. It's a lab: every rule that
decides what "the same place" means on a world that changed is a toggle
( rules ), and the log says what happened and why.

Arrows or WASD, or swipe. Space pauses, . takes one step, V zooms out (ride, far, high, the whole world; + and −, a wheel or a pinch fine-tune), Shift+A hands it to the autopilot. Tap a note to dismiss it.
